result:
The proposed answer of ∞ is wrong.

The cycle argument fails because the claimed lower bound on spread is false. A cycle C_n has a path decomposition of width 3 in which every vertex lies in at most 4 bags. Use bags like {v_i, v_{i+1}, v_{n-i}, v_{n-i+1}}, which sweep inward from both ends of the cycle. So for any c ≥ 3/2, the cycles satisfy the spread condition with a constant c'. The pigeonhole argument claiming some vertex must persist over Ω(log n) levels is not valid.

Since the cycle counterexample fails, the set of c for which P(c) fails is not all of ℝ. As I recall (from memory, not re-derived here), the known result is that every graph has a tree decomposition of width at most about 2·tw(G)+1 with s(v) ≤ d(v)+1, and that no constant c < 2 works. That would give α = 2, not ∞.

VERDICT: REJECT
